newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Croat general goes on trial for Bosnia war crimes.
newsitem.headline: Croat general goes on trial for Bosnia war crimes.

text.p: A Bosnian Croat general on Tuesday became the highest-ranking suspect to go on trial at the U.N. war crimes tribunal in the Hague.

General Tihomir Blaskic, 36, appeared before the court charged with crimes against humanity committed against Moslems in the Lasva Valley area of central Bosnia from 1992 to 1994, when he was a colonel commanding Bosnian Croat (HVO) militia forces in the area.
The tribunal says Blaskic led a campaign of ethnic cleansing in the area, with hundreds of civilians killed during the razing of Moslem villages.
The indictment alleges grave breaches of the Geneva Conventions governing conduct during wartime, violations of the laws and customs of war, as well as crimes against humanity.
Blaskic voluntarily surrendered to the tribunal in April 1996 and has been held under house arrest at a secret Hague location since then. He has pleaded not guilty to all charges.

He was a career officer in the federal Yugoslav army before the country's break-up, holding the rank of captain. In 1992 he became a colonel in the Bosnian Croat militia and was advanced to general in 1994.

Blaskic was promoted to a senior post in Croatia's regular army after his indictment for war crimes and decorated by Croatian President Franjo Tudjman for his war service, drawing international criticism.
